evidence.exact_quote: Acceptance criterion AC-08 requires UI/workflow state to normalize deterministically into the canonical runtime mode enum before strategy selection, and Interview, BrainStorm, and Crew must not create additional runtime mode values.

items.impact: Implementations can deterministically choose different mappings for the same UI/workflow state, especially for unknown, stale, or combined workflow values, while still claiming compliance.
items.statement: The criterion fixes ordering and prohibits enum growth, but it does not define the complete UI/workflow-to-runtime mapping, precedence for combined states, or rejection/fallback behavior for unmapped states.
items.title: UI workflow normalization lacks a total mapping

evidence.exact_quote: Acceptance criteria AC-09 and AC-10 require regular mode with dae disallowed to fall back to HTE while persisting regular_dae_disallowed, and yolo with dae disallowed to fail before provider spawn with yolo_requires_dae_provider rather than silently downgrading.

items.impact: The regular and yolo branches have distinct, observable, falsifiable outcomes and prevent a dangerous silent downgrade in yolo.
items.statement: The DAE-disallowed policy is explicitly split by mode, persists the regular fallback reason, and requires yolo failure before provider spawn.
items.title: DAE policy branches are explicit and testable

evidence.exact_quote: Policy denials, FileSafe blocks, UI-only terminal actions, and different shell fingerprints MUST NOT increment the same streak.

items.impact: Concurrent attempts or inconsistent fingerprint implementations can merge or split streaks differently, producing nondeterministic kill decisions.
items.statement: The exclusion set is preserved, but the canonical fingerprint algorithm, counter partition key, atomic update rule, and boundary behavior for the sliding window are not defined here.
items.title: Kill counters lack concurrency and partition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Acceptance criteria AC-14 and AC-15 preserve terminal identity behavior: Open in Terminal and Show Terminal reveal the existing terminal_session_id when available, explicit restart or replacement mints a new terminal_session_id, and clear-scrollback/reveal-only actions preserve current runtime identity.

items.impact: Simultaneous reveal and restart/replacement requests can reveal a stale session, mint duplicate sessions, or attach the UI to an identity different from the active runtime.
items.statement: Identity preservation and minting are specified, but stale-session detection, serialization of competing actions, and the observable result when the referenced session disappears during reveal are not.
items.title: Terminal reveal and replacement races are undefined

evidence.exact_quote: Run modes do not replace shared failure_class or blocked_reason_code taxonomy; failover reason codes hard_exhaustion_failover, auth_failure_failover, workspace_deactivated_failover, model_unsupported_failover, and provider_unhealthy_failover remain stable in reason_codes or owning runtime/audit envelopes, and mode changes do not rewrite original failover reasons.

items.impact: Failure provenance remains stable across mode changes and can be audited without conflating policy state with provider failover state.
items.statement: The unit explicitly preserves the shared failure taxonomy and forbids mode changes from rewriting original failover reasons.
items.title: Failover reason continuity is preserved

evidence.exact_quote: Headless ask denial remains explicit and non-magical: when tool policy resolves to ask and no interactive approval path exists, headless_ask_denied is blocked/denied rather than auto-retry, and blocked outcomes do not count as qualifying writes or retryable provider errors.

items.impact: Headless denial cannot inflate retry or write-thrash counters and cannot silently enter an automatic retry loop.
items.statement: The headless ask path has an explicit blocked classification and explicit counter exclusions.
items.title: Headless denial counter semantics are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime safe points are required only for mutation-capable attempts: ask/plan remain read-only and need no mutation safe points for ordinary planning or inspection, while regular/yolo create safe points before risky mutation-capable attempts; addendum acceptance preserves retry taxonomy, explicit headless denial, blocked-counter exclusions, and safe-point creation by execution authority.

items.impact: Different builders can classify the same mutation as risky or non-risky and legitimately omit rollback protection for destructive actions.
items.statement: The unit binds safe points to execution authority and mutation capability, but it does not define the risk predicate that decides which mutation-capable attempts require a safe point or the required behavior when safe-point creation fails.
items.title: Safe-point applicability leaves the risk predicate open

evidence.exact_quote: All Assistant Chat modes operate within the active thread worktree when one is bound: Ask reads, Agent edits, Plan/Deep Plan executes plans, and Debug targets the worktree; mode transitions do not change worktree binding because binding is thread-level, not mode-level.
ask/plan remain read-only and need no mutation safe points for ordinary planning or inspection

items.impact: A builder can interpret Plan/Deep Plan as mutation-capable execution even though the nearby run-mode rule says plan remains read-only, widening authority without a clear transition.
items.statement: The phrase 'Plan/Deep Plan executes plans' is not reconciled with the adjacent requirement that plan remain read-only; the label-to-runtime-mode mapping and mutation authority boundary need an explicit distinction.
items.title: Plan execution wording conflicts with read-only plan semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree commands cmd.chat.worktree.* remain available in all modes subject to when-clauses, and the worktree header button and dropdown menu are always visible regardless of current mode.

items.impact: The always-visible control can appear actionable when its command is disallowed, with inconsistent disabled, hidden, or explanatory behavior across surfaces and assistive technologies.
items.statement: Visibility is fixed and command availability is conditional, but the unit does not specify the button/menu disabled state, reason presentation, keyboard behavior, or accessible labeling when a when-clause fails.
items.title: Always-visible worktree controls lack unavailable-state truth

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime mode affects immediate recovery affordances but not blocked classification: interactive modes may present auth/approval/clarification, headless modes yield blocked_reason_code=headless_ask_denied, later mode/prerequisite changes may resume by creating a new attempt snapshot without rewriting original blocked classification, and restore-before-rerun safe-point policy still applies.

items.impact: Recovery can proceed without destroying historical classification, and rerun cannot bypass required restoration.
items.statement: The blocked-to-resumed transition creates a new attempt snapshot, preserves the original blocked record, and retains restore-before-rerun policy.
items.title: Blocked recovery preserves immutable history

evidence.exact_quote: Deferred/waiting run semantics keep a run active while any node is runnable; if no node is runnable but blocked, backoff, or prerequisite-waiting work remains, the run is deferred/waiting rather than terminal, and terminal completion requires no runnable, blocked, backoff, or unresolved prerequisite work.

items.impact: Permanently blocked, lost-wakeup, or unreachable-prerequisite runs can remain active forever without a deterministic escalation, cancellation, or support signal.
items.statement: The terminal predicate is explicit, but wakeup ownership, backoff ceilings, prerequisite loss, offline behavior, deadlock detection, and operator cancellation for indefinitely deferred runs are not specified.
items.title: Deferred runs have no liveness or abandonment contract

evidence.exact_quote: Headless blocked discovery emits blocked_notice with blocked_reason_code=headless_ask_denied, surfaces blocked node count in CLI/log or dashboard summaries when available, includes the exact missing permission or approval, and returns status unavailable with reason headless to tool and operation-card consumers when no interactive presenter exists.

items.impact: CLI, logs, dashboards, tools, and operation cards can disagree on counts and reasons, especially when several nodes require different permissions or approvals.
items.statement: The consumer outcomes are named, but the blocked_notice schema, multi-blocker representation, count availability requirement, ordering, deduplication, and update/clear behavior are not defined.
items.title: Headless blocked notices lack a multi-consumer payload contract

evidence.exact_quote: If a UI session is attached, headless blocked discovery may surface a dashboard badge or notification; headless contexts must not offer GUI-only recovery actions such as Open in Terminal and must instead provide resume guidance, permission-preset adjustment, interactive mode change, allowed fallback strategy, orchestrator-facing blockage, or abort guidance.

items.impact: An attached UI may give no visible indication of a blocked headless run, and different builders can choose different recovery guidance without a priority or eligibility contract.
items.statement: The prohibition on GUI-only recovery is strong, but 'may surface' leaves attached-session notification optional and no lifecycle, accessibility, localization, deduplication, or stale-badge clearing oracle is provided.
items.title: Attached UI blockage signaling remains discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: Run modes do not redefine mutation_capable: the tool registry declares mutation_capable bool default false, the node planner propagates it into node plans, and modes only control whether mutation-capable attempts may occur and therefore whether safe points are relevant.

items.impact: A newly registered, malformed, or adversarial mutation-capable tool that omits the flag can be treated as non-mutating, bypassing mode gating and safe-point protection.
items.statement: Because mutation_capable defaults to false, omission is safety-significant; this unit provides no fail-closed registration validation or invariant proving that every mutating tool is explicitly classified before use.
items.title: Default-false mutation classification can fail open

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime identity and blocked-policy continuity require execution_role, requested_account_id, operational_identity, account-switch and pressure ownership, blocked_sequence minting and persistence, startup recovery rehydration/handshake, unchanged DAE jail/approval policy ownership, usage switch-history, and usage execution-role follow-through across mode changes and blocked recovery; cov-159 exact item markers remain lineage evidence.

items.impact: Crash recovery or concurrent account/mode changes can rehydrate a mixed identity-policy snapshot, duplicate or reorder blocked sequences, or attribute usage to the wrong account or role.
items.statement: The required continuity fields are enumerated, but snapshot versioning, atomic persistence, precedence during concurrent changes, blocked_sequence uniqueness/ordering, handshake idempotency, and partial-rehydration rollback are unspecified.
items.title: Runtime identity recovery lacks an atomic snapshot contract

evidence.exact_quote:
Discovery/configuration/GUI availability is not permission to mutate, attach, expose ports, push images, inject
  secrets, use remote hosts, or certify completion. Blocked host outcomes such as permission_denied, filesafe_blocked,
  runtime_disabled, runtime_unavailable, capability_unavailable, host_untrusted, host_unreachable, and test_gap_policy
  remain `blocked != failed`.

items.impact: The same multi-cause host incident can receive different primary states, retry behavior, and user guidance, or remain blocked indefinitely after the underlying condition clears.
items.statement: The authority boundary and blocked-not-failed rule are explicit, but precedence among simultaneous blocked reasons, retryability, unblock detection, state transition after recovery, and receipt requirements for those transitions are not defined.
items.title: Host blocked outcomes lack precedence and recovery transitions

evidence.exact_quote: GUI consumers render streaming_partial, failed, adjusted, blocked, unknown, and settled distinctly and do not treat blocked != failed runtime outcomes as zero usage or final settled cost.

gui_related: false
gui_classification_reason: Run-mode outcome semantics feed GUI projections but are backend policy/state contracts.

items.impact: GUI-specific assurance, ownership, accessibility review, and visual-state fixtures can be skipped even though the PlanUnit contains mandatory user-visible rendering behavior.
items.statement: RM-049 is classified gui_related false while its canonical text and acceptance criteria directly require distinct GUI rendering and drill-through behavior; the classification conflicts with the normative surface contract.
items.title: Usage projection is misclassified as non-GUI

segments.summary: Reviewed RM-033 through RM-044 line by line across normalization, provider fallback, counters, terminal identity, taxonomy continuity, headless denial, safe points, worktree behavior, blocked recovery, deferred liveness, and consumer status truth. Strong non-gaps coexist with material mapping, race, authority, liveness, and GUI-state gaps.

Reviewed RM-045 through RM-049 and every intervening core line, including migration/retired-bridge context and compile addenda. The strongest risks are optional attached-UI signaling, fail-open mutation classification, non-atomic identity recovery, incomplete blocked-host recovery semantics, and a contradictory GUI classification.
